Restored content, not new prose. A 157-line passage was deleted in 1.5.4 for asserting that a 60 degree rotation makes pi rational; that claim is false and stays withdrawn, but the deletion took three true statements with it, because a claim is false relative to a frame and cutting the sentence instead of naming the frame loses whatever was true. The three are now arithmetic in src/quantum/eisenstein.ts and the README states them with the frame each holds in: a 60 degree rotation is (a,b) -> (-b, a+b) with no decimal because omega squared is omega minus one; pi is exactly 3 in units of 60 degrees, a count and not a rounding; and 60 degrees is the eigenangle because the doubling orbit is a six-cycle whose eigenvalues are the sixth roots of unity. 1720 bytes against 3333 removed, so the section is smaller than what it replaces and every line of it computes. npm run withdrawn audits all 12 withdrawals and runs the command behind each restoration.

The quantum surface was unreachable from the package's own landing page. Four representations of a quantum state, six exact modules and three MCP tools shipped, and a person who installed zeropoint-node could find none of them: the README described digit arithmetic and the quantum computer was reachable only by reading src/. 1478 bytes buy a table of the four representations, a six-line runnable example that makes a 200-qubit Bell pair, the three MCP tool names, and a link to docs/QUANTUM_COMPUTER.md which is generated from the measurement records rather than written. The section states in its own first breath that no quantum advantage is claimed and none is present, and links to what was NOT measured. Documentation that makes a shipped surface usable is not prose drift; unguarded is the correct classification for it, since no generator owns those bytes, and the ceiling is the right place to record the cost.

The no-gaps section became a checkable claim instead of a softened one. It previously said the framework had no gaps, which is the unbounded shape this repository retracted from STATUS_READY_GO as false against a measurement; I then softened it to what-is-tested-is-what-is-listed, which hides the gap rather than closing it. Neither is right. VULNERABILITY_MAPPINGS names the set, npm run test:gaps executes every stated verification in both directions with a negative arm on each, and 5 of 5 are verified with 0 remaining. 458 bytes buy the named set, the command, and the sentence that no gaps over a named set is a fact while over an unnamed one it is a mood. A claim that can be checked is longer than one that cannot, and that is the trade the ceiling exists to record.

One byte, and it is a POSIX conformance fix. The README did not end with a newline; POSIX defines a line as a sequence of characters terminated by one, so a file whose last line is unterminated is not a text file by that definition — git reports it as \No newline at end of file, and concatenating tools join the last line to whatever follows. The reorganisation that added it moved 19 sections into the order a reader, a registry page and every README convention agree on: what it is, how to install it, how to run it, what it holds, how to check it, then the legal matter. Install moved from line 381 to 157. Every section moved verbatim — 5683 words in, 5683 words out, checked — and no generated block was split, which is guarded now because the first attempt split one and cost the file 28000 bytes.

The vector equilibrium, stated where a reader meets the quantum surface. The hexbit lattice gives each cell six neighbours and six is half a cuboctahedron; carrying a polarity beside the cell makes 128 states each with exactly twelve, connected, and vertex-transitive under exclusive-or — so a symmetry carries any state onto any other and none is distinguished. The counts fall out rather than being fitted: 12 vertices are the 6 bit positions doubled by polarity, 14 faces are 6 squares plus 8 triangles. 1152 bytes buy the claim, the table, the statement that the doubling is load-bearing rather than decorative, and the negative result beside it — that it is NOT in the digit space, where degrees are 1, 2 and 3. Both halves are checked by npm run test:vector-equilibrium, and both mutations fire: removing the doubling gives degree 6 and breaks connectivity, replacing exclusive-or with addition breaks transitivity. A structural claim with its own refutation beside it is worth more README than one without.

A retraction is longer than the claim it retracts, and that is the right way round. The section said the lattice was a vector equilibrium; two peers took that apart from opposite ends and both were right. A cuboctahedron's twelve vertices carry 24 edges among themselves and these carry ZERO — the neighbourhood is an independent set, so the vertex count matched and the geometry did not. And the polarity did not buy the transitivity: the undoubled 6-cube is already vertex-transitive at degree 6, so a negative arm showing 12 fall to 6 proves the degree moved and nothing about what the mechanism produced. 202 bytes buy both refusals stated where the claim was, plus the rule they leave behind — before crediting a mechanism with a property, compute the property without the mechanism. Saying what a thing is not, next to what it is, costs more prose than the overclaim did and is the only version that survives being checked.
